, in the crayfish, 5-HT has a dual role, depending on its origin, the animal’s social status, and its mode of action.

5-HT is able to produce both excitatory and inhibi-tory effects on MNs of isolated crayfish, but the balance between these two effects can be shifted by the social status of the animals, as well as by the type of 5-HT application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-HT neurons can be involved in both excitation and inhibition of MN activity in the crayfish motor network, depending on the 5-HT receptor type, as well as the MN type.
5-HT can be considered as a neuromodulator that can either enhance or inhibit the activity of the motor network, depending on its mode of application.

the duality of responses of crayfish MNs is not due to the activation of two different 5-HT receptors, but rather to the differential distribution of 5-HT receptor subtypes in different compartments of a single MN, as well as to the differential distribution and density of 5-HT terminals in the neuropil.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 5-HT-evoced duality in crayfish locomotor networks can be reproduced by activation of 5HT cells, and that the diversity of effects can be explained by spatial segregation of 2 different 5-HT receptors, namely the 5-HT2A and the 5-HT7 receptors.
the diversity of effects of 5-HT on crayfish MNs can be reproduced in vivo by the activation of single 5-HT neurons.
